transcript:
APPROVED ON NOVEMBER 4, 2026

# REGULAR MEETING OF THE SOUTH BURLINGTON SCHOOL BOARD

Wednesday, October 21, 2026
Executive Session at 5:00 p.m.
Regular Session at 6:00 p.m.
South Burlington School District Administrative Office
577 Dorset Street, South Burlington, VT

## REGULAR MEETING

### PRESENT

Seamus Abshere, Jennifer Lawrence, Dan Boyer, Michelle Boyer, Elissa Galvez, Emilee Hoffman

### ADMINISTRATION/STAFF

Dr. Joe Clark

### GUESTS

None

### Call Regular Meeting to Order

Seamus Abshere called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.

### EXECUTIVE SESSION

The Board convened in Executive Session at 5:31 p.m.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to enter executive session at 5:31 p.m. to discuss employment of a public officer or employee, labor negotiations, and receiving confidential attorney-client communication for the purpose of providing legal services to the Board as permitted under Vermont law and added that it would be significantly disadvantageous to the district not to do so in executive session.

Jennifer Lawrence moved, and Michelle Boyer seconded. All in favor; motion passed.

Topics of discussion included employment of a public officer, confidential attorney-client communication for the purpose of providing legal services to the Board, and labor negotiations.

IN: 5:31 p.m.
OUT: 5:57 p.m.
No Action

Dan Boyer moved to adjourn the executive session at 5:57 p.m. Michelle Boyer seconded. All in favor; motion passed. The executive session was adjourned at 5:57 p.m.

The Board returned to the regular meeting at 6:01 p.m.

## SCHOOL BOARD MINUTES — PAGE 2

## REGULAR MEETING

### PRESENT

Seamus Abshere, Jennifer Lawrence, Dan Boyer, Michelle Boyer, Elissa Galvez, Emilee Hoffman, Tom Chittenden (arrived 6:58 p.m.), Oliver Kunz, Momin Waqar

### ADMINISTRATION/STAFF

Dr. Joe Clark, Jean-Marie Clark, Nicole Carter, Daisy Brayton, Suzanne Gruendling, Lissa McDonald, Polly Vanderputten, John Craig, Keith Terry

### GUESTS

Alex McHenry, Student Emilia, Student Grady, SPARC consultants Matthew, Shannon, and Noah

### Call to Order

Seamus Abshere called the meeting to order at 6:05 p.m. The Pledge of Allegiance was said.

## ANNOUNCEMENTS AND AMENDMENTS TO THE AGENDA

### Announcements

The Board confirmed the following Board members would be attending the Vermont School Boards Association (VSBA) and Vermont Superintendents Association (VSA) Annual Conference on October 30, 2026 in Burlington as Dr. Joe Clark, Jennifer Lawrence, Michelle Boyer, and Elissa Galvez.

The Act 170 Merger Committee recently met, with Seamus Abshere representing South Burlington School District, Claire Wohl representing Burlington School District, and Nicole Mace representing Winooski School District. It was decided that Burlington would have three voters, South Burlington would have two voters, and Winooski would have one voter. The next meeting will be November 2, 2026 and Seamus Abshere and Dan Boyer will attend to represent the South Burlington School District.

### Amendment to Agenda

It was agreed by the Board to amend the agenda and to not review the Consent Agenda items Accounts Payables, Payroll Warranties, and Accounts Payable Voucher Checks, as warned, and to move those items to the next scheduled meeting on November 4. They were incorrectly added to the agenda.

### Comments and Questions

Alex McHenry approached the Board and talked about October being Domestic Violence Awareness Month. He urged anyone experiencing domestic violence to reach out to support agencies.

There were no questions.

## SCHOOL BOARD MINUTES — PAGE 3

## Focus on Student Learning

### Student Representative Report

Oliver Kunz shared that parent-teacher conferences were taking place this week.

Momin Waqar mentioned the end of the first quarter will be October 30 and for students to check their grades before the quarter ends. There will be a food drive at the high school to benefit the high school food pantry and Dorset Street Food Shelf.

Oliver Kunz shared how Frederick H. Tuttle Middle School (FHTMS) recently completed their One School, One Book reading of Buster's Day. Girls and boys varsity soccer teams have advanced to the tournament championships and varsity field hockey earned a win over Browns River.

Momin Waqar said the boy's cross-country team took first place and the girl's cross-country team earned second place at the Chittenden County Championships held recently at the Shelburne Museum. He mentioned that cross-country will compete again this week, padded flag football has a game this week and how students and staff are preparing for the upcoming winter sports season.

Momin Waqar said middle school students were staying busy with various councils, leadership groups, and clubs and that high school playoffs were all starting this week.

There were no questions.

### South Burlington High School Student Presentation

**The Board agreed to move forward with next agenda items until students arrived.**

## DISCUSSION ITEMS

### Monthly Financial Update

Jean-Marie Clark explained how purchase orders were being better encumbered by staff. She noted the cost of fuel and working with the transportation team to be even more efficient when using buses. Some money that was potentially set aside to have work done outside of the diesel mechanic, will be shifted into the fuel budget line. She felt the District was in pretty good shape, even though it is still a bit early in the year to discuss revenues.

She expects to receive feedback around December from the auditor's annual review that was done in October.

There was some discussion about the school budget being fluid; the importance of submitting purchase orders correctly; how the District was being even better in its processes and stricter with how money was being spent; and how there was not currently an identified emergency fund separate from the capital reserve fund that could be unlocked by voters.

There were no questions.

## SCHOOL BOARD MINUTES — PAGE 4

### Policy F4 Investigation and Response to Harassment, Hazing, and Bullying of Students (Second Reading)

Joe Clark created and emailed the Board a redline version of the document; to clearly show the current policy compared to what is being recommended by the Agency of Education. Seamus Abshere asked if the redline version could be posted in public documents for the public to see as well.

There were no questions.

### Policy D9 Electronic Communications Between Employees and Students (Second Reading)

Joe Clark created and emailed the Board a redline version of the document for better clarity about what the expectations are between staff members and students, and the boundaries that should exist between students and staff members regarding electronic communication, as recommended by the Agency of Education. Seamus Abshere asked if the redline version could also be posted in public documents for the public to see.

There were no questions.

### The Other Paper Article Production Process

There was some Board discussion whether the District pays for the opinion page space in The Other Paper, as they are the paper of record for South Burlington. It was noted how the space had only been used a few times over the past few years and how the Board has been doing some really good things and how this could be the opportunity to capture that work. Joe Clark offered to find out what the parameters were for the space and to provide that feedback back to the Board. The District's production schedule was discussed and how to collaboratively write items, without violating open meeting laws.

Michelle Boyer shared a specific comment from the community survey feedback that suggested a quarterly, or at least a few times a year, article from the Board communicating with the public highlighting the status of things. There was some additional discussion about what that might look like. It was agreed by the Board that Jennifer Lawrence and Michelle Boyer would put together the initial 12-month timeline draft and would present an update at the next Board meeting.

There were no questions.

### Act 170 Merger Committee Report from October 20th First Meeting

Seam Abshere provided another brief update (first mentioned in the Announcements section) about the first meeting held on October 20. He explained the reason for the merger committee and how it differed from CESA, the Chittenden Central Cooperative Educational Service Area. He discussed representation from each district and how the Winooski School Board Chair was elected to be the chair of the merger committee. The next meeting was scheduled for November 2 and then again December 7; with the committee planning to meet on a monthly basis. Meeting dates will be posted on their website. Seamus Abshere and Dan Boyer will be attending the next meeting as representation for South Burlington.

## SCHOOL BOARD MINUTES — PAGE 5

Michelle Boyer was in attendance of the October 20 meeting and further defined the proportionality among districts to the Board.

There were no questions.

**The high school students arrived and the Board agreed to proceed with student presentations.**

### South Burlington High School Student Presentation - The International Experience (TIE)

Lissa McDonald (Principal, High School) said the presentation would talk about two exchanges that were just completed. She provided an overview of the program, traveling locations both internationally and domestically, experiences being in the program, and exchanges.

Student Grady noted that he did the TIE Germany program a few years ago. He read aloud the speech he had presented to the 9th and 10th graders encouraging them to check out TIE, which included his own "amazing experience". He described his experience as profound, independent, perspective, connection, and an experience of a lifetime.

Student Emilia hosted for the Germany, French, and Spanish exchange. She talked about having friends all over the world and staying in touch with those she had hosted in the past. She has had a great experience with the program.

Polly Vanderputten (TIE Coordinator) mentioned how they just had several weeks of visitors from Spain and Germany. She noted that she was a SBHS graduate and did not do the exchange program when she was in high school because her family could not afford it. She would like to see it made more broad as an offering to students. There were student alumni invited that could not attend so she read their comments aloud to the Board. The comments were positive, and described wonderful experiences, memories, and life-long friendships. Polly noted multi-generational aspects, connections between families and other cultures. She also shared a comment from a recent first time host parent of an exchange student who tied the experience to the district's Ends policy. The hosting parent felt grateful to be part of the experience.

Lissa McDonald invited the Board to visit the website to see student photos, videos, testimonies, and student journals from their travels.

Jennifer Lawrence shared some of her personal experiences with the program. She also understood the financial aspect and wondered if there would be an opportunity to create some kind of scholarship program for students; maybe some fundraising that might be explored down the road.

There were no questions.

**The Board agreed to switch the order of agenda items ACTION ITEMS and SUPERINTENDENT'S REPORT to accommodate visiting SPARC consultants to present next.**

## SCHOOL BOARD MINUTES — PAGE 6

## SUPERINTENDENT'S REPORT

Joe Clark explained how the Strategic Plan process had started and a consultant had been chosen through the Request for Proposal (RFP) process.

The consultants provided an overview of the firm, noting they were a Vermont-based firm. Their team was introduced as Shannon a social psychologist, Matthew a sociologist, and Noah a project manager. They mentioned how community engagement was underway, with strong initial participation. The planning process will use a combination of an Open Planning Committee, a smaller Steering Committee, and additional stakeholder groups to review existing data, identify priorities, and develop a draft strategic plan.

A key theme throughout the discussion was the importance of ensuring that the final plan reflects the community's priorities, including meaningful accountability measures, and that it remains a living framework for decision-making, budgeting, and ongoing evaluation.

The initial Open Planning Committee meeting reviewed the Board's existing Ends Policy and used discussions, small and large group conversations, and dot voting to identify questions, concerns, and priorities. The consultants explained how they will use the existing data gathered by Joe Clark rather than duplicating prior research, and will share drafts with him throughout the process. The goal is to have a draft plan ready to share by December. Participants emphasized how the plan should be easy to understand and practical to use. The consultants will develop the middle layer connecting the Board's vision to implementation by Joe Clark; while budgeting, staffing, and operational implementation will remain the responsibility of the school district.

Board members raised the importance of measuring progress and demonstrating that the planning process leads to meaningful action. Joe Clark emphasized that the strategic plan must belong to the community, not to him personally. The consultants reinforced that strategic planning is about creating a framework for making decisions, not merely producing a written plan. Board members stressed the importance of ensuring that participation reflects the broader community, including groups that may be underrepresented. The consultants acknowledged the importance of representative participation and had already suggested engaging additional groups, including student council and PTA.

There was some discussion about student involvement and what that might look like and how community members can contact the consultants between meetings.

There were no questions.

## ACTION ITEMS

### Monitoring Report 2.3 Treatment of Community

Joe Clark presented the first internally conducted monitoring report for the Treatment of Community policy. The report was intended to establish baseline data for future annual

comparisons and to further assess how effectively the district recognizes community members as stakeholders in school programs and facilities.

Joe Clark explained how the community survey received 143 responses from families and other community members, including outreach through Front Porch Forum and other communication channels. He said that because comparable historical data was unavailable, the results were considered preliminary baseline data rather than a scientific longitudinal assessment. While there were many district performance improvements, Joe Clark acknowledged that opportunities remain to improve communication, build trust, and ensure that community members understand how to participate in district decisions. He rated the district as approaching compliance, recognizing substantial progress while identifying opportunities to strengthen engagement practices and accountability systems.

Board members expressed support for Joe Clark's thoughtful approach, the collection of baseline data, and efforts to broaden community participation. Discussion highlighted several opportunities such as, improving visibility on the district's website, using annual property tax communications, collaborating with the City of South Burlington, and exploring broader community use of school facilities.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to monitor Monitor Report 2.3 Treatment of Community using the monitoring rubric included in the Board materials. Tom Chittenden moved, Emilee Hoffman seconded. No discussion. All in favor; motion passed.

## CONSENT AGENDA

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to approve the bid for snow removal and salting. Emilee Hoffman moved and Dan Boyer seconded the motion. There was a question why the contract was for only two schools and Joe Clark said because the contract gets smaller and smaller every year as the district attempts to do more and more in-house. All in favor; motion passed.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to approve the bid for rubbish and recycling. Emilee Hoffman moved and Tom Chittenden seconded the motion. No discussion. All in favor; motion passed.

Seamus Abshere asked if there were any objections to the Consent Agenda. Hearing none. Agenda is passed by consent.

## AGENDA FOR NEXT MEETING

The following items were added to the November 4 agenda:

- Tour of SouthPoint at 577 Dorset Street (5:30 p.m.)
- The Other Paper Article Calendar and Production Process
- Executive Limitations Revision
- Act 170 Merger Committee Update from November 2 Meeting
- Budget Process and Schedule *(Joe Clark)*

## ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, Seamus Abshere called for a motion to adjourn. Tom Chittenden moved and Jennifer Lawrence seconded. Motion carried unanimously and the meeting adjourned at 8:04 p.m.
